profile.headline: Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I am a software engineer experienced in developing full-stack applications in the React/Node.js/TypeScript architecture, using both SQL and NoSQL to create new software solutions. Currently an active contributor of Chronos, an open-source monitoring tool for all applications, where we built the feature for AWS monitoring. I also recently spoke at the Jeeny + Bractlet Tech Talk Series on developing single page applications with React Router.

Check out more of my work at:
https://github.com/timlee12

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Enabled Amazon Web Service (AWS) monitoring for clusters, containers, and instances running on its ECS/EC2/EB platforms, connecting to AWS CloudWatch through the AWS-SDK for Node.js

Utilized Electron to develop a React/Node.js/Chromium desktop application, creating a secure local sandbox environment to visualize metrics and fetch backend data with native inter-process communication methods

Developed React components with the TypeScript superset, assigning types/interfaces onto components throughout the application to give the JavaScript codebase static typing for greater reliability before runtime

Applied Docker to containerize Express-developed test applications, creating an image-based microservice testing environment to scrape metrics from deployments equipped with Chronos’ native npm dependency

Compiled SQL and NoSQL databases to store metric statistics for containerized applications, giving users multiple data storage solutions to persist information needed to store and receive accurately documented data

Employed Jest testing on components by implementing React Testing Library to create unit and integration testing, improving coverage by 25% and ensuring a smooth and efficient CI/CD pipeline with Travis CI

Implemented Material-UI and Plotly to create a dynamically responsive and visually appealing user interface, rendering pre-packaged, fully built React components and customizable graphs to display fetched data

Chronos is an open-source product maintained by the tech accelerator, OSLabs.

positions.title: Software Engineer | Quietude - Study Location Tracking Web Application
positions.description:
Employed Axios to send asynchronous HTTP requests to REST APIs developed with Node.js/Express, using middleware to interact with and manipulate user and location data from a schema-defined NoSQL database

Connected with third-party APIs (Google Maps, Yelp) to access location data and render map components onto the application interface, giving users a visual representation of local study locations on the dashboard

Designed with Tailwind to create a responsive user interface, using CSS markup language directly in React components for ease of use, greater readability, and an overall quicker development process

positions.title: Software Engineer | AppliTrack - Career Application Management System
positions.description:
Integrated Google OAuth2.0 into the user validation process, ensuring secure login and access control for protected user resources, and improving UX by enabling single, one-tap sign-in functionality 

Architected and deployed a PostgreSQL database management system for relational data between multiple schemas, resulting in optimized, ACID-compliant storage and retrieval for necessary application data

Implemented Redux to give the React application a single source of truth for its state, centralizing the state for all components and containers, resulting in improved performance, maintainability, and scalability

positions.title: Software Engineer | LearnAxolotl - Environment Wildlife Education Platform
positions.description:
Applied React Router to create a responsive single-page application capable of client-side routing, enhancing user experience and overall performance with dynamic navigation between multiple endpoints

Built frontend with React to create modular, reusable components, enabling easy modification and faster rendering times, while also enabling client-side state management with React hooks
